task: Airway mucociliary clearance: ciliary-beat (CBF) + two-layer periciliary-sol/mucus-gel transport quantitative model, geometrically derived (low-Re two-layer lubrication + viscosity-switch scallop-theorem-breaking argument), forced against a CBF-only geometry-blind adversary.
confidence_tier: literature-anchored, multi-source over-determined (16 PMID/DOI citations, every one live-verified via NCBI eutils this session; zero recalled-and-trusted)

core_falsifier.pre_registered_threshold: healthy trachea velocity in [4,10] mm/min, using CBF+PCL-geometry inputs independently measured (no fit to the velocity anchor); CBF-velocity relationship linear; PCD (CBF->0) abolishes clearance; CF (periciliary depletion, CBF UNCHANGED) impairs transport via geometry alone, and a CBF-only adversary forced to its strongest fair form must FAIL to reproduce CF.

pcd_adversary_test_non_discriminating.real_anchor_afzelius1976: no mucociliary transport measured by tracheobronchial clearance; cilia lack dynein arms (PMID 1084576)
pcd_adversary_test_non_discriminating.note: PCD does NOT discriminate the two models -- both correctly predict abolition when f=0. The discriminating test is CF (3.5).

sweep.real_anchor_matsui1998: CF epithelia: abnormally high ASL absorption depleted the PCL and ABOLISHED mucus transport (PMID 9875854)
sweep.real_anchor_rutlandcole1981: CF vs controls: no significant CBF difference; nasal clearance in CF significantly slower (p<0.001, n=10/group); 'innate function of cystic fibrosis cilia, as measured in vitro by beat frequency, is normal' (PMID 7314040)

cf_adversary_forcing_test_the_central_re.verdict: CBF-only adversary predicts 0.0% change in CF (structurally cannot respond to periciliary geometry); forced geometric model predicts 84.4% reduction at an illustrative severe-collapse point -- matching the qualitative direction of Matsui 1998 ('abolished mucus transport') and Rutland & Cole 1981 (CBF normal, clearance abnormal in real CF patients). General/class-level result: ANY CBF-only model is logically excluded by Rutland & Cole's single measurement that CF's own CBF is unchanged.

symmetric_qc_distal_slowdown_not_explain.interpretation: CBF is essentially INVARIANT across trachea/mainstem/basal-segment (both temperature groups, n=30, paper's own reported p>0.05) -- this REFUTES a naive 'CBF simply declines distally' explanation for the well-known slower-distal mucus transport. The real mechanism (airway cross-sectional geometry / regional rheology / shorter-range metachronal coordination in smaller airways) is an honest, disclosed OPEN gap, not modeled quantitatively here.

overdetermination_theory_vs_measurement.honest_reading: Two fully independent, decorrelated sources (a 1986 two-layer Newtonian lubrication-theory calculation with no biological input, and a 2012 dextran-exclusion microscopy measurement) both place the physiologically-relevant depth ratio in the same narrow high-x sub-unity band -- genuine over-determination, NOT an exact numerical bullseye (Button's 0.929 sits ~9% outside Fulford-Blake's tighter 0.80-0.90 optimum, on the shallow-penetration side, which Fulford-Blake themselves note is 'not essential' for positive transport).

coordination_illustrative_not_independen.description: Metachronal coordination (Sanderson & Sleigh 1981, PMID 7263784: antiplectic traveling waves of coordinated beating) is modeled as a THIRD, logically independent multiplicative efficiency term kappa (kappa=1 implicit in the Sears-2015 calibration, since their tissue had normal coordination). This is NOT independently quantified with a fresh number this session (disclosed gap) -- shown only to illustrate that a dyskinetic-but-normal-frequency defect (kappa low, f normal) is a THIRD way, structurally distinct from both PCD's f->0 and CF's x-collapse, for a CBF-only adversary to fail.

decorrelated_anchor.description: Multiple independent, non-tautological external anchors -- none is a re-statement of the model's own output.
decorrelated_anchor.anchor_1_trachea_velocity: Foster/Langenback/Bergofsky 1980 (PMID 7380708) tracheal mucus velocity 4-10 mm/min, radiolabeled-marker measurement -- fully independent of the CBF (Yager/Chilvers) and PCL-depth (Button) inputs used to compute the model's prediction.
decorrelated_anchor.anchor_2_theory_vs_measurement: Fulford & Blake 1986 (PMID 3796001, pure lubrication theory, no biological data) vs Button 2012 (PMID 22923574, dextran-exclusion microscopy, no theoretical input) converge independently on the same high-x optimal-depth band.
decorrelated_anchor.anchor_3_disease_cohorts: Camner/Mossberg/Afzelius 1983 (PMID 6604650, n=20 PCD vs n=8 non-PCD, real clearance measurements) and Rutland & Cole 1981 (PMID 7314040, n=10/group, real CBF+clearance measurements in CF) -- neither dataset used to calibrate any model parameter, both used purely as held-out falsifiers.
decorrelated_anchor.never_a_tautology_gate: The healthy-point prediction (6.63 mm/min) uses three calibration numbers (f0, x0, d_per_beat) sourced from FOUR separate papers, none of which report a trachea mm/min velocity themselves -- the 4-10 mm/min check is a genuine out-of-sample comparison, not a circular restatement.

honest_gaps: Foster et al 1980's own exact mm/min figures were not independently re-extracted from primary text (pre-abstracting-era, no abstract retrievable) -- 4-10 mm/min used as the task's own given band, bibliographically anchored to the correct classical paper.

CF's own exact periciliary-depth collapse (microns or x=delta/L) was not independently measured/re-extracted this session -- Matsui 1998's abstract is qualitative only ('depleted', 'abolished'); the CF test is an illustrative severity sweep, not a point-asserted number.

alpha (recovery-stroke profile height fraction) is a disclosed illustrative parameter, not independently pinned to one verified number -- mitigated (not resolved) by a 7-point robustness sweep, all passing.

Metachronal coordination (kappa) is illustrative only -- no quantitative coordination-efficiency number was independently verified this session (targeted searches returned no hits); a dyskinetic-normal-frequency PCD subtype is mentioned as a known clinical concept but not backed by a fresh citation this session.

The 'slower distally' mechanism is an open gap -- CBF-decline was tested and REFUTED as the explanation (Yager 1980, real data), but the actual quantitative mechanism (airway geometry / regional rheology / shorter-range coordination) is not modeled.

Partial common-mode risk: Sears 2015 and Button 2012 (the two most load-bearing calibration numbers) both originate from the UNC Chapel Hill CF/pulmonary research center, though via methodologically distinct measurements -- disclosed explicitly at section 11 (over-determination), where the non-exact ~9.2% gap is reported rather than hidden.

Mucus rheology (psi) is a simple linear calibration to one paper's one concentration sweep (Sears 2015, 2-8% mucin) -- real mucus rheology (shear-thinning, viscoelastic, pH/hydration-dependent) is far richer than this single-axis term.

0-D/population-averaged model: no explicit spatial PDE re-solve of the Fulford-Blake lubrication problem, no cilium-length/PCL-depth population variance, no explicit metachronal-wave spatial simulation.
